Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/86box.git...

Analyzing 86box AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines two sources hosted on GitHub under the official 86Box organization: the main application source and an assets archive, both pinned to version 6.0 via tagged releases. These sources are fetched using HTTPS, and while checksums are provided (sha512sums), even if they were skipped, that would not make this stage unsafe — the purpose of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` is to download and extract sources for auditing.

The global scope of the PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, depends, etc.) with no command substitution, external execution, or network activity. There is no `pkgver()` function defined, so no dynamic version calculation occurs. As a result, sourcing the PKGBUILD during this phase performs no actions beyond parsing static metadata and preparing for source retrieval.

No code in the top-level scope or in functions that would be evaluated during sourcing (such as `pkgver()`) executes dangerous operations. The `build()` and `package()` functions are irrelevant here due to `--nobuild` and `--noprepare`. Thus, running the specified makepkg commands will safely fetch and extract the declared sources without executing any untrusted code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No dangerous execution during source fetch</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No dangerous execution during source fetch

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by the Arch User Repository (AUR) to describe the package build configuration for `86box`. It lists standard fields such as package name, version, architecture, dependencies, sources, and checksums. The sources point to official GitHub release tarballs under the project's own repository (`https://github.com/86Box/...`), which is expected and appropriate. Both source archives are accompanied by `sha512sums`, indicating strong cryptographic verification of the integrity of the downloaded files — there is no use of 'SKIP' here, so checksums are enforced.

No executable code or scripts are present in this file. The content consists purely of declarative package metadata, with no commands, downloads, or system modifications. All dependencies listed are reasonable for an emulator application, including GUI, audio, input, and networking libraries. Optional dependencies reference related packages in the AUR (e.g., `86box-roms`, `discord-game-sdk`) but do not introduce any external or untrusted download sources. There are no signs of obfuscation, suspicious URLs, or unauthorized network activity.

The package follows standard AUR packaging practices and shows no evidence of tampering or malicious injection. While the sources track specific Git tags (v6.0), which could in theory be repointed (though unlikely on GitHub), the presence of correct and non-skipped SHA-512 checksums ensures that any modification would be detected during build. This constitutes a safe and verifiable build process.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR metadata with verified sources; no malicious content
</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/2] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR metadata with verified sources; no malicious content
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build and packaging process for the 86Box emulator, sourced from its official GitHub repositories. The sources are fetched from `https://github.com/86Box/86Box` and `https://github.com/86Box/assets`, which aligns with the project's upstream. The checksums are provided as sha512sums, ensuring source integrity. There are no skipped checksums, and the sources are pinned to a specific tag (v6.0), enhancing reproducibility.

The build process uses CMake in a conventional manner, setting appropriate flags and install prefixes. It compiles the application and installs it into the package directory. The packaging step includes installing icons and a desktop file following freedesktop.org conventions, and copying sound assets to the correct shared location. All operations are confined to the build and package directories, with no attempts to access network resources, execute external scripts, or modify system files outside of `$pkgdir`.

No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized system modifications are present. The dependencies and optional dependencies are reasonable for an emulator with multimedia and hardware emulation capabilities. The maintainer metadata is properly formatted, and there are no signs of injected malicious logic.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR package with clean build and safe sources
</summary>
</security_assessment>
